memory_update.text: COHR and LITE should be retained as reference leaders for AI InP photonics, lasers, and data-center optical components; they anchor the node but are not the primary underfollowed alpha lane.

VECO is a high-priority underfollowed Layer 1B candidate because official company evidence directly links its MOCVD, ion-beam deposition, and wet-processing orders to InP laser manufacturing and optical interconnect demand.
ALMU may remain in the speculative shadow lane only if later filings confirm commercial AI photonics or communications customers, wafer-scale manufacturability, and repeat revenue.
Need a follow-up pass on US-listed optical test, wafer bonding, photodetector, and inspection suppliers; current evidence is strongest for lasers/InP device makers and MOCVD/IBD equipment.
COHR and LITE should be retained as high-attention reference anchors for AI optics capacity, InP ramp, and strategic customer validation, but not treated as underfollowed discovery names.
VECO is a stronger underfollowed Layer 1B candidate because it maps directly to MOCVD/InP epitaxy equipment, a plausible upstream bottleneck behind AI optical interconnect scaling.
ALMU belongs in speculative_shadow rather than core underfollowed until AI datacenter product qualification, commercial revenue, named customers, and scalable yield evidence are verified.

Next searches should expand beyond U.S.-listed names to foreign ordinaries/ADRs for MOCVD, etch/deposition, bonding, inspection, and optical test suppliers, because several key process-equipment chokepoints may be non-U.S.-listed.
VECO is a high-priority underfollowed equipment candidate for the compound_photonics_cpo_stack node because disclosed InP laser tool orders directly match the bottleneck hypothesis.
AEHR should be tracked as a qualification/test-gate candidate for silicon photonics, optical I/O, and CPO; survival depends on repeat customer orders and material revenue contribution.
ALMU belongs only in the speculative_shadow lane until commercial qualification, wafer-scale yield/reliability, and named customer revenue are verified.
COHR provides scaled InP/AI optics context, but it should not crowd out smaller upstream tool, test, and alternative-platform candidates in this pass.

Still need a separate pass for US-listed optical manufacturing services, bonding tools, plasma etch/deposition, substrates, and distributors; Fabrinet, MKS, Onto, and related names were not included due to the four-candidate limit.

VECO should be tracked as an underfollowed equipment candidate in the AI optical-interconnect stack because it has announced $250M+ of InP laser manufacturing equipment orders tied to 800G/1.6T and hyperscale data-center optics.
AXTI should be tracked as a small-cap InP substrate candidate, but it needs current verification on InP capacity expansion, backlog, customer qualification, and China/export-control risk.

ALMU belongs in the speculative_shadow lane as a potential III-V-on-silicon bypass of native InP constraints; keep it out of higher-confidence layers until commercial revenue, yield, and customer qualification are verified.

For compound_photonics_cpo_stack, the underappreciated choke points appear to be InP substrate/device capacity, InP laser manufacturing equipment, MOCVD/ion-beam/wet-processing tools, and manufacturable III-V-on-silicon alternatives rather than only transceiver brands.

Need a follow-up pass on US-listed optical test, inspection, precision bonding, and CPO assembly/yield tools; this pass found stronger immediate evidence for InP substrates and InP laser manufacturing equipment.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the AI optical-interconnect and compound-photonics chokepoint. The clearest direct-exposure names are Coherent and Lumentum as InP photonics and AI data-center optical component leaders. Veeco enters the underfollowed equipment lane because recent company disclosures tie its MOCVD, ion-beam deposition, and wet-processing tools directly to InP laser manufacturing and silicon-photonics optical interconnect demand. Aeluma is included only as a speculative shadow candidate because its III-V-on-silicon platform could be relevant if native InP wafer capacity remains constrained, but commercial qualification, revenue scale, customer concentration, and manufacturability require verification. Layer 1B expansion for the AI optics/CPO manufacturing stack. The reference lane is now strongly validated by NVIDIA's 2026 strategic optics investments in Coherent and Lumentum, suggesting hyperscalers and AI accelerator vendors are treating optical interconnect capacity as a strategic supply-chain input. The underfollowed lane should focus on equipment and platform suppliers that sit upstream of transceiver brands: MOCVD/InP epitaxy tools, III-V-on-silicon approaches, etch/deposition/bonding/test capacity, and receive-side photodetector platforms. This is research-support only, not a trading recommendation. Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the compound-photonics/CPO manufacturing stack.
